newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia blocks Croat-Serb ceasefire line meetings.
newsitem.headline: Croatia blocks Croat-Serb ceasefire line meetings.

text.p: Croatia on Saturday closed down a market serving as a meeting point for Croats and Serbs from the enclave of Eastern Slavonia for what they called health reasons.

The state news agency HINA quoted Osijek-Baranja county authorities as saying the market on the U.N.-secured ceasefire line was shut to prevent a spread of livestock disease beyond the Serb-controlled enclave.
They said two people needed medical help for stomach ailments after attending the market a few days ago.
UNTAES, the U.N. transitional administration in Eastern Slavonia which is to revert to Croatian government rule next year, was unhappy with the Croatian decision.
"Such moves are contrary to confidence-building measures and can only slow down peaceful reintegration," UNTAES said in a statement.

HINA said the market would be sealed off from the Croatian side "until UNTAES provides minimum hygienic conditions for gathering of great numbers of people, inspection of meat and unimpeded work of sanitary and veterinarian workers."
UNTAES, trying to defuse mutual Croat-Serb suspicions by encouraging trade and social contact, organised an initial market gathering on a neutral stretch of road in August.
Only 200 people turned up then, but crowds at the weekly event have since grown to 8,000.

Eastern Slavonia is Croatia's last separatist Serb enclave, one of three taken in a 1991 minority revolt against Croatia's move to independence from Yugoslavia. The other two were recaptured in Croatian army offensives last year.
The Croatian parliament has demanded that the United Nations not extend UNTAES' mandate when it expires in January.
But the U.N. Security Council is likely to renew the mandate for three months to allow more time for Croat-Serb reconciliation.

Many of the estimated 130,000 Serbs in the region remain opposed to the restoration of Croatian authority but no longer have the military means to prevent it as UNTAES disarmed their militia last spring.
